title: Brain-motor behavior coupling during walking while negotiating obstacle: A systematic review
title_zh: 行走中障碍物规避的脑-运动行为耦合：系统综述
abstract: Obstacle negotiation is a complex walking task requiring sensory integration, motor planning, and executive control. Understanding its neural mechanisms may improve insight into mobility impairments. This systematic review investigated cortical activity and gait performance during obstacle negotiation across different populations using a brain-motor behavior framework. PubMed and Web of Science were searched up to April 2025 following PRISMA guidelines. Studies including adults performing obstacle negotiation with concurrent functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and gait assessments were eligible. Findings were interpreted as neural compensation, neural inefficiency, or capacity limitation. Thirteen studies (n = 649) involving individuals with Parkinson's disease (PD), stroke, older adults, and young adults were included. Most studies assessed prefrontal cortex (PFC) activity. Increased PFC activation with impaired gait performance was common in PD, stroke, and older adults, supporting the neural inefficiency model. In contrast, increased PFC activation with preserved gait performance in healthy young and older adults suggested neural compensation. A few studies showed unchanged cortical activation despite gait deterioration, indicating neural capacity limitation under demanding conditions. Task characteristics, such as unanticipated obstacles and dual-task conditions, were associated with further increases in PFC activation. Cortical control of obstacle negotiation is influenced by task demands, neural reserve, and methodological factors. Executive cortical resources appear critical for adaptive walking across populations, whereas neurological populations and older adults more frequently exhibit neural inefficiency or capacity limitation when gait performance deteriorates. Future studies should investigate additional cortical regions to further elucidate the neural mechanisms underlying adaptive walking.
abstract_zh: 障碍物规避是一项复杂的行走任务，需要感官整合、运动规划和执行控制。了解其神经机制可能有助于深入理解运动障碍。本系统综述采用脑-运动行为框架，调查了不同人群在障碍物规避过程中皮层活动与步态表现的关系。根据PRISMA指南，检索了截至2025年4月的PubMed和Web of Science数据库。纳入条件为：成年人在进行障碍物规避时同时使用功能近红外光谱（fNIRS）和步态评估。研究结果被解释为神经补偿、神经低效或容量限制。共纳入13项研究（n = 649），涉及帕金森病（PD）、中风、老年人和年轻成人。大多数研究评估了前额叶皮层（PFC）的活动。PFC激活增加且步态表现受损在PD、中风和老年人中较为常见，支持神经低效模型。相反，PFC激活增加且步态表现保持良好的健康年轻人和老年人提示神经补偿。少数研究显示，尽管步态恶化，皮层激活保持不变，表明在高负荷条件下存在神经容量限制。任务特征，如突发障碍物和双任务条件，与PFC激活进一步升高相关。障碍物规避的皮层控制受任务需求、神经储备和方法学因素的影响。执行性皮层资源似乎对跨人群的适应性行走至关重要，而神经疾病人群和老年人更频繁地表现出神经低效或容量限制，尤其在步态表现下降时。未来研究应进一步探讨其他皮层区域，以阐明适应性行走背后的神经机制。
